content.body:
The next evolutionary step from the A15 Crusader II was meant to be the Cavalier. The failure of that program left the British military searching for some way to get 6pdr/57mm guns in the field to cope with the heavier German tanks that were showing up more frequently in North Africa. Taking the quickest solution, they gave the Crusader chassis another upgrade and stuffed a 6pdr gun into the turret. As an expedient, the Crusader III was quite successful although woefully thin by comparison to the armour of the German tanks it faced.
Control Variations: Driver spawns in with view slit armor in place, can zoom on open viewslit (numpad . or Del key). Key O opens bigger view window, driver can also zoom on this view (numpad . or Del key). Gunner does not have view slit. The gunner has a range setting only visible by pressing the tilda (~) key.
Functionally almost identical to the previous Crusader II, the Crusader III is a better tank now with a gun capable of killing most German AFV's. The green color and main armament make it excellent from ambush, although the characteristically weak British optics somewhat negate the range advantages of the QF.6pdr gun. It remains very lightly armored, particularly on the later-war context. Drive it like an armored car pay close attention to your situation and don't stand and fight anything without moving to your advantage. Don't be afraid to stop and look around, as long as youre in cover; the green coloring will hide you from cursory examination.
As we saw with the Crusader II, you need to fear air attack, your roof/deck armor can be penetrated even by fighter machineguns. You can lure enemy panzers closer to see if you have actually despawned in the event that you are disabled but not on fire, the color of your camouflage sometimes makes it hard to pick you out at range.
content.brief: TYPE: Medium AFV ARMAMENT: 57mm Main Gun (QF.6pdr) 1 x .303 inch MG WEIGHT: 20085 kg SPEED (road): 43 km/h
